title: Chicken Thighs in Mushroom-Thyme Yogurt Sauce
summary: Seared thighs finished in a white wine and mushroom pan sauce, made creamy with Greek yogurt and Parmesan.

ingredients.note: or 1 1/2 cups chicken stock and skip the water

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Pat the thighs dry and season with salt and pepper, ideally an hour ahead.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Sear in the oil over medium-high without crowding until deeply browned, about 4 minutes a side. They finish in the sauce. Set aside with their juices.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.text: Add the butter and mushrooms. Spread them out and leave them alone before stirring so they brown instead of steam. Cook until deep brown and dry.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add the shallots, garlic, and thyme and stir until fragrant.

steps.title: Reduce the wine
steps.text: Pour in the wine, scrape up the fond, and reduce by at least half. This keeps the acid from splitting the yogurt later.

steps.title: Finish the chicken
steps.text: Add the stock and water, return the chicken and juices, cover, and simmer gently until the thighs reach about 175°F.

steps.title: Stabilize the yogurt
steps.text: While it simmers, whisk the yogurt with the cornstarch until smooth. The starch keeps the yogurt from curdling.

steps.title: Temper and finish off the heat
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat. Whisk a ladle of hot sauce into the yogurt, then stir it into the pan. Add the Parmesan a handful at a time. Don't let it boil again. Taste, then salt and add lemon if it needs lift.

notes: Made with beef stock cut with water and 1/2 cup Parmesan; it leans toward stroganoff and comes out browner. Beef stock and Parmesan are both salty, so salt only at the end.
